messages:
incident-bot: [automated] Canary healthcheck FAILED: service=runtime-gpu region=us-east-1 rollout=v3.0.0-canary rate=10%

maria: i'm getting paged - grabbing console. called into this one. @tom can you join?

tom: oncall handoff acked. pulling logs and heap metrics now. any customer reports yet?

rachel: product saw a tiny uptick in 502/504 on streaming endpoints around 09:02-09:06. no public tickets so far but one customer slack DM about intermittent timeouts.

maria: seeing pod OOMs on a subset of canaries -> CrashLoopBackOff then bursts of retries. suspect memory regression or config change.

tom: i can kill the canary flag if needed. feature flag: canary_toggle_v3. do we want an immediate kill-switch?

rachel: yes please. minimize customer impact. do a graceful kill if possible so streams don't drop hard.

maria: issuing kill now.

maria: @deploy-bot set-feature-flag canary_toggle_v3 false --reason="OOMs on canary" --scope=us-east-1
deploy-bot: acknowledged. Feature flag canary_toggle_v3 set -> false. Canary traffic halted and routed to stable v2.9.6.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1769994321 | Canary memory regression during deploy. Severity: P2. Assigned: maria, tom.

tom: rollback triggered by flag flip. kubectl command to rollback in case we need explicit undo:
```
kubectl -n runtime rollout undo deployment/runtime-gpu --to-revision=34
```

maria: rolling back and scaling stable up. monitoring health.

deploy-bot: traffic switched to v2.9.6. healthchecks passing.

rachel: note: our alert noise made triage harder — we got both canary-err-rate and endpoints-5xx alerts, fired at different times, and an infra pod-crash alert. unclear primary signal.

maria: agreed. also couldn't see per-canary heap usage in the canary dashboard; the memory-by-instance panel is missing for this deployment group. that delayed root-cause confirmation.

tom: i couldn't find the kv-cache hitrate panel for the new model variant either. without that we can't assess cache pressure vs memory leak.

rachel: SLO confusion: the 99th latency SLO metric showed a small burn but our SLO alert didn't include deploy window annotations so we weren't sure if it was deploy-caused or a user-facing regression.

maria: action for observability: 1) restore memory-by-instance panel to canary dashboard, 2) add per-variant kv-cache metrics, 3) annotate deploy windows automatically on SLO dashboards.

tom: collecting artifacts now: heap dumps + journalctl from failed pods, saving to incident bucket. commands run:
```
PODS=$(kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=runtime-gpu -o name | grep canary)
for p in $PODS; do kubectl -n runtime exec $p -- tar czf /tmp/logs-$p.tgz /var/log /var/heapdumps || true; kubectl -n runtime cp $p:/tmp/logs-$p.tgz /tmp/ || true; done
aws s3 cp /tmp/logs-*.tgz s3://redwood-incidents/1769994321/
```

tom: uploaded artifacts to s3://redwood-incidents/1769994321/

support-bot: FYI posted a proactive support note to #support: "We paused a canary for v3.0.0 due to memory regressions; routing remains on stable. Monitoring and rollback complete; reaching out if you see issues."

rachel: good. follow-ups: infra to check dependency diffs between v2.9.6 and v3.0.0 (maybe a libc bump?), eng-runtime to add CI canary memory checks, obs to consolidate duplicate alerts into a single incident-priority alert, and SRE to add deploy annotations.

maria: i'll own the incident doc and initial postmortem. tom, please attach heap dumps and any heap profiler traces. i'll schedule a quick postmortem sync in 1 hour.

tom: will do. ticket INC-2026-1769994321 updated with artifacts and timeline.

deploy-bot: Thread closed by deploy-bot.
